gaps.explanation: 'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: Smoke could be seen ___ from the factory chimneys.
gaps.hint: the smoke goes up by itself — no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (no object) describes the smoke going up; 'raise' would need an object (raise something).

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She studied ___ for her final exams.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning with a lot of effort
gaps.explanation: 'Hard' is an adverb meaning with great effort ('work hard'); 'hardly' means almost not at all.
